2.3 Parity bits

Even parity

A parity bit is one extra bit sent with a group of data bits so the receiver can notice a single flipped bit. With even parity, the sender picks the extra bit so the total count of ones is even.

The parity bit of n data bits is their exclusive OR: p = d1 ⊕ … ⊕ dn

Detecting errors

The receiver recounts the ones. An odd count means some bit flipped on the way; an even count means no single-bit error happened, though two flips cancel out and go unnoticed.
